title: The Azure-Clad Visitor
next_chapter_hook: Su Qingyao's figure vanished into the depths of the bamboo grove, leaving only words that sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine — 'Your father once asked me the same question.' The familiarity in that tone made Chen Ji feel, for the first time, a chill beyond the chessboard.

text.content: Night wind passed through the bamboo grove at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, producing rustling sounds like countless departed souls whispering. Chen Ji sat upon a blue stone, his fingers unconsciously stroking the fragmentary Tianji Record hidden in his sleeve. Since the conclusion of the third scroll, he had gone seven consecutive days without closing his eyes. Not from vigilance, but because that premonition grew stronger — something was approaching him. The runes on the fragment occasionally flickered with faint blue light, indicating the Tianji Record sensing surrounding Spiritual Energy fluctuations. Starting seven days ago, this blue light appeared with increasing frequency. Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his mind: 'Boy, the one you've been waiting for has arrived.'

The footsteps were very light, almost completely masked by the sound of bamboo leaves. But Chen Ji still heard them — not with his ears, but with the instincts honed during seven years as a废物. His fingers tightened slightly, then relaxed, a faint weariness spreading across his face, as if merely a servant disciple awakened by nightmares. 'It's late night, why doesn't the Junior Sister rest in the Inner Sect? What brings you to enjoy the wind at the back mountain?' His voice carried lazy indifference, not even lifting his head. Amid the swaying bamboo shadows, a blue-clothed figure stopped ten paces away.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Senior Brother is in high spirits. Alone at this hour, sitting in such a place — if I hadn't passed by, I might have thought you were having a secret meeting with something.' That voice was cold as spring water, yet carried an unnoticeable undertone of inquiry. Only then did Chen Ji raise his head, his gaze falling upon the visitor's face. Blue garment, long hair, cold features — precisely Su Qingyao, the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of the Tianqing Sect. Unlike her rumored ice-cold image, there was now a hard-to-read light in her eyes.

text.content: Su Qingyao walked closer, her embroidered blue skirt dragging细微声响 across the stone slabs. Her gaze swept across Chen Ji, lingering briefly on his sleeve before moving away. That momentary pause was almost negligible, but Chen Ji caught it. Her nostrils twitched slightly, as if distinguishing some scent. 'The Inner Disciple Senior Fellow personally visits the back mountain — this humble Chen is merely a small servant disciple, unworthy of such honor.' Chen Ji stood, clasped his hands in salute, his movements impeccable, his humility perfectly calibrated.

dialogue.content: 'Enough.' Su Qingyao raised her hand to stop him, her gaze直视 Chen Ji's eyes. 'You and I both know this etiquette is meaningless to you. Chen Ji, I came to ask you something.' Her tone was flat, yet carried an unavoidable pressure. 'Three months ago, the Elder guarding the Scripture Pavilion suddenly went berserk, his meridians completely severed. You just happened to appear near the Scripture Pavilion that night. I want to know what you saw.'

text.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened slightly. The events of three months ago, of course he remembered. That night he was indeed present — precisely speaking, he had seen the scene three hours later in the Tianji Record: the Elder would be corrupted by demonic energy, go berserk, and the source of that demonic energy pointed precisely toward a direction he had yet to ascertain. He intervened beforehand, leading that demonic energy away, yet hadn't expected Su Qingyao to still catch his trail. This woman's nose was sharper than he imagined.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's probe came earlier and more directly than anticipated. She knows about the Scripture Pavilion Elder incident, clearly not without basis. How should you respond?

choices.text: Pretend ignorance to probe her cards
choices.description: Since she knows more than imagined, first see exactly how many cards she holds, then decide the next move. The废物 persona must be acted out to the end — let her show her cards first.
choices.visible_reward: Find out Su Qingyao's information source
choices.risk_hint: If she's merely bluffing, proactively revealing information will backfire

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes flickered with confusion, then transformed into panic: 'Scripture Pavilion? Three months ago? Junior Sister is enlightened — I'm merely a servant disciple, I can't even enter the Scripture Pavilion, how could I see anything—' He deliberately lowered his voice, his gaze capturing every细微表情 change on Su Qingyao's face.

choices.description: Since concealment isn't possible, might as well give her part of the truth. Can dispel her hostility while using her power to investigate the demonic energy source — after all, the enemy of an enemy can be a temporary friend.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Su Qingyao's partial trust and demonic energy clues
choices.risk_hint: Too much honesty may make her more vigilant; too little will be seen as perfunctory

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then slowly spoke: 'That night... I did see something. The Scripture Pavilion Elder had a strand of demonic energy, not his own. I tried to stop it, but whose voice as a servant disciple would be heeded?' A bitter smile crossed his face, his gaze perfectly displaying a mixture of helplessness and unwillingness.

choices.description: She can precisely find her way here, meaning she's had her eye on you for some time. Rather than being passively beaten, take the initiative — let's see what this Inner Disciple Senior Fellow truly wants, coming alone to the back mountain at night.
choices.visible_reward: Seize dialogue initiative, understand her true purpose
choices.risk_hint: Being too forceful might turn her into an enemy from now on.

text.content: Chen Ji's smile slowly faded, the layer of cowardly disguise peeling away like a mask. "Younger sister comes alone in the deep night, just happening to 'pass by' the place where I always sit—such keen eyesight truly impresses Chen. I'm just curious—" He stepped forward, the distance between himself and Su Qingyao suddenly narrowing. "Did you come to ask questions, or to silence me?"

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's pupils contracted slightly, clearly not expecting him to be so direct. But the next moment, the corner of her lips actually lifted in an extremely faint curve: "Interesting. It seems the rumored waste Chen Ji is indeed not as simple as he appears on the surface."

text.content: The wind in the Bamboo Grove suddenly stopped. Su Qingyao's gaze lingered on Chen Ji's face for a moment—devoid of the previous coldness, replaced by a sharpness that surveyed prey. "There's a trace of demonic energy residue on your sleeve, very faint, so faint that the Inner Sect elders couldn't detect it. But I can." Her words were like a soft blade, seemingly casual yet striking straight at the vitals. "You can discover the source of that demonic energy, can't you?"

dialogue.content: "The source of that trace of demonic energy didn't come from outside—it came from deep within the forbidden area on the seventh floor of the Scripture Repository." Su Qingyao's voice dropped lower. "There's an ancient relic sealed there, leaking a wisp of demonic energy every sixty years. But three months ago, that leak occurred a full thirty years earlier than it should have. I've searched the sect records, and nothing explains this anomaly." She stared into Chen Ji's eyes. "Until I caught the distinctive scent of that relic on your sleeve."

text.content: Chen Ji's heart skipped a beat. The seventh-floor forbidden area—he had never been there personally. The Tianji Record had indicated the demonic energy source pointed in that direction, but he hadn't dared enter recklessly. A servant disciple entering the seventh floor of the Scripture Repository was a capital offense in itself. He had drawn away that demonic energy from the outside, relying on the foresight ability the Tianji Record granted, combined with his precise judgment of spiritual energy flow. But Su Qingyao could actually smell the forbidden relic's essence from his sleeve—this woman was far more dangerous than he had imagined.

However, what alarmed him even more was another matter. Su Qingyao said that relic "leaks once every sixty years"—this meant her knowledge of the forbidden area far exceeded that of ordinary Inner Sect disciples. The authority of an Inner Sect Senior Fellow couldn't possibly extend to accessing the seventh-floor forbidden area. She either had other information channels, or... she herself had some connection to that relic. Chen Ji quickly ruled out several possibilities in his mind and temporarily set this thread aside. Now was not the time for deeper investigation.

dialogue.content: "Who exactly are you?" Su Qingyao suddenly asked this question, her voice carrying the first trace of wavering. "Regarding the timing of the forbidden area's seal loosening three months ago, only three people in the entire Tianqing Sect knew—only the Sect Master, my father, and the Scripture Keeper Elder at the time. My father and the Scripture Keeper Elder are both dead; the Sect Master wouldn't leak information to a servant disciple. So how did you know?"

text.content: Su Qingyao's father—Chen Ji quickly caught this piece of information. Su Qingyao's father was already dead, killed in an "accident" ten years ago. And the Scripture Keeper Elder had gone berserk three months ago. Two people, two key知情者, one dead and one crippled. The connections between them were far more complex than they appeared on the surface. Su Qingyao had come to him in the deep night, ostensibly to inquire about the Scripture Repository, but in reality—she was investigating the true cause of her father's death. The "accident" ten years ago, the forbidden area anomaly three months ago—these two threads had converged at this "waste" Chen Ji.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's true face was gradually revealing itself—she was not merely a tester, but an investigator with her own agenda. A subtle intersection of interests had formed between you, yet both sides still had reservations. How might one steer this conversation in a more favorable direction?

choices.description: Su Qingyao is investigating her father's death, while you are investigating the mastermind behind the forbidden area's demonic energy. Your enemies likely point to the same person. Now is the time to extend an olive branch.
choices.visible_cost: Expose more information to the other party.
choices.visible_reward: Gain a powerful ally—Su Qingyao's intelligence network opens to you.
choices.risk_hint: She might be using you, and the consequences of being exposed are severe.

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then made a move that surprised Su Qingyao—he slightly turned aside, allowing the moonlight to illuminate his features. On that ordinarily meek face, an expression she had never seen before emerged—deep and profound. "Younger sister, you wish to know the truth of your father's death ten years ago, and I wish to know the true cause of the forbidden area anomaly three months ago." His voice was soft, yet each word rang clear. "If we cooperate, perhaps we can find the answers we both seek."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's breath barely perceptibly caught. She clearly hadn't expected this waste servant disciple to lay his cards on the table so directly. But the next moment, the surprise in her eyes transformed into something more complex—scrutiny, calculation, and a faint hint of appreciation. "You know my father?" Her voice dropped even lower, nearly audible only to the two of them.

choices.text: Only exchange information, don't expose your trump cards.
choices.description: Cooperation is possible, but there's no need to show all your cards. Give her a taste, test the depth of her sincerity—the existence of the Tianji Record must never be revealed.
choices.visible_cost: Unable to obtain Su Qingyao's complete trust.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain your own air of mystery, seize the information advantage in subsequent negotiations.
choices.risk_hint: She might consider you insincere, refusing further cooperation.

text.content: Chen Ji gently shook his head: "I don't know who your father is, but I know the true purpose of that surge of demonic energy three months ago—it wasn't a leak, but a search for something." He lowered his voice. "That relic is calling out to its other half. And that other half is not in the Scripture Repository." He didn't mention the existence of the Tianji Record, but this statement alone was shocking enough.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's expression slightly shifted. She clearly hadn't expected this answer. "The other half..." she quietly repeated the word, her gaze suddenly becoming much more complex. "Are you saying—that relic is searching for the Tianji Record?"

text.content: Chen Ji's heart sank violently, but no change crossed his features. He merely smiled faintly, as if commenting on an unimportant joke: "The Tianji Record? What's that? I only said the other half lies with the one who sealed that relic. Ten years ago, your father perhaps knew the answer."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao stared at Chen Ji for a long time, long enough for the wind in the bamboo grove to pick up again. Finally, she spoke, her voice carrying an strange calm: "When my father was dying, he only told me two things. The first was 'Heavenly secrets must not be revealed,' and the second was—'Find the person with the surname Chen.'" Her gaze fixed on Chen Ji. "I always thought he meant some Chen family elder or some Chen family senior. It wasn't until three months ago, when the Forbidden Grounds became abnormal, that I discovered—among all the Chen family elders, only Chen Xuan—your father—had entered the seventh level of the Forbidden Grounds ten years ago."

text.content: Chen Xuan. Chen Ji's father, who died fifteen years ago in an 'accident.' The same as Su Qingyao's father, who also died in an 'accident.' Two fathers, two causes of death, two buried secrets, all revealed tonight by the same woman. Chen Ji felt the fragment in his sleeve grow slightly warm—that was the Tianji Record responding to his emotional fluctuations. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind: "Kid, your father is more complicated than you know. And she knows more than she thinks she does."

The night grew deeper, moonlight filtering through the bamboo leaves and casting mottled shadows on the ground. Su Qingyao stood there quietly, waiting for Chen Ji's response. Her eyes were calm, but beneath that calm was a storm accumulated from ten years of obsession. Chen Ji suddenly smiled—not the sycophantic smile of a废物, nor the bitter smile of a servant, but a genuinely relieved smile tinged with desolation. "My father died fifteen years ago," he said. "Su Junior Sister's father died ten years ago. Yet your father, on his deathbed, told both of them to find the same 'person with the surname Chen.'" He lifted his gaze, revealing his true emotions for the first time—neither cold calculation nor scheming, but something interwoven with deep-seated pain and longing. "You're right. Our enemies are likely the same person."

Su Qingyao's breathing noticeably quickened. The answer she had pursued for a decade finally revealed its first crack tonight. And the person who provided this crack was unexpectedly the sect's infamous废物 servant. The irony made her want to laugh, but she held back. "Who is that person?" Her voice tightened. Chen Ji shook his head: "I don't know. But I know one thing—the demonic energy three months ago wasn't naturally released. Someone deliberately opened the seal's gap." He paused. "And there are no more than three people in the Tianqing Sect who could open that gap."

Su Qingyao's pupils constricted. She understood Chen Ji's implication. The person who could open the Forbidden Grounds seal three months ago had been narrowed to extreme limits—the Sect Master, the Grand Elder, and... the deceased Tower Guardian Elder himself. The Tower Guardian Elder's 'loss of control'—was it because someone silenced him? Then, who had the ability and motive? The night wind rose again, Su Qingyao's long hair floating in the breeze. Her expression became unprecedentedly grave. "Chen Ji," she said, for the first time using an equal tone rather than a condescending one, "are you willing to cooperate with me?"

This was the most crucial question of the night. Not about the Scripture Library, not about the Forbidden Grounds, but about trust. Su Qingyao had spent ten years investigating alone, and tonight she chose to speak to a servant disciple—this in itself was a tremendous concession. Chen Ji looked at her, at the hardships hidden beneath that cold face, and suddenly understood something. This woman, like him, had walked alone in the darkness for too long. They trusted no one, yet at this moment, chose to trust each other.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao formally extended a cooperation invitation. This was the first time Chen Ji received a genuine olive branch from the Inner Sect—though the other party didn't yet know all his cards. How should he respond?

choices.text: "Reveal everything and establish a deep alliance"
choices.description: "Since her father and my father point to the same幕后黑手, there's no need to hide anymore. Reveal everything about the Tianji Record in exchange for her unwavering trust and support."
choices.visible_cost: "The risk of the Tianji Record's secret being exposed is extremely high"
choices.visible_reward: "Gain Su Qingyao's complete trust and intelligence network, and unlock the 'Shared Fate' prerequisite"
choices.risk_hint: "Once she leaks it or gets captured, the consequences would be unimaginable"

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and made a decision even Mo Xiansheng hadn't anticipated. He took out the fragmented Tianji Record from his sleeve and handed it to Su Qingyao. "This is my trump card." His voice was very light, light as a falling leaf. "The reason I could foresee the abnormality in the Forbidden Grounds three months ago isn't because I have some special ability, but because of this."

dialogue.content: The moment Su Qingyao took the fragment, her fingers trembled violently. The flowing runes on that page were exactly as described in the notes left by her father—"Tianji Divine Guidance, Peering into Fate and Seizing Heaven." Her eyes suddenly reddened, but no tears fell. "So that's how it is..." Her voice was somewhat hoarse. "So the 'person with the surname Chen' my father told me to find wasn't looking for a specific person, but... the inheritor of the Tianji Record."

text.content: Chen Ji nodded. He looked at Su Qingyao's reddened eyes and suddenly felt something touch a corner of his heart. Ten years. This woman had investigated alone for ten years. And he himself, hadn't he done the same? The wind in the bamboo grove seemed to grow gentler at this moment. "From now on," he said, "we are allies."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao returned the fragment to Chen Ji, her fingertips lingering on the paper's surface for a moment—that was the thing her father had sought until his death, now lying before her. She looked up; moonlight fell on her face, and that cold expression gained the first hint of warmth. "In three months, the Forbidden Grounds will face the true Jiazi Great Calamity. At that time, the seal will completely collapse." She looked at Chen Ji. "And we must find the answers before then."

text.content: Chen Ji nodded. He knew this was a game he had to play. The more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the deadly backlash of fate—Mo Xiansheng's warning still echoed in his ears. But if he didn't act, the Jiazi Great Calamity three months later would swallow the entire Tianqing Sect. His fingers gently traced the runes on the fragment, feeling the power flowing within. Su Qingyao's addition meant he had another pair of eyes, another intelligence line, and also something... he was unwilling to admit. Under the moonlight, two people who had walked alone in the darkness for years chose to stand side by side for the first time. The bamboo leaves rustled, as if witnessing this silent pact.

choices.description: "Cooperation is possible, but boundaries and exchange conditions must be set. You need substantive gains from her—intelligence, authority, or protection—rather than empty promises."
choices.visible_reward: "Gain her intelligence network and resource support without exposing the Tianji Record"
choices.risk_hint: "Setting conditions too high will appear lacking in sincerity"

text.content: Chen Ji didn't answer immediately. He looked at Su Qingyao, moonlight casting two cold lights in his eyes. "Cooperation is possible." He said. "But I have conditions." Su Qingyao slightly raised her brow, indicating for him to continue. Chen Ji raised three fingers: "First, I want to be informed of all clues you find about my father. Second, you'll find a way to secure a spot for me to enter the seventh level of the Forbidden Grounds in three months. Third—" his voice suddenly became very light, "no matter what happens, you must never tell anyone that I possess the Tianji Record."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao was silent for a moment. Chen Ji's three conditions, the first two were within reason, but the third—he deliberately emphasized the secrecy of the Tianji Record, indicating that thing's importance to him far exceeded her imagination. She recalled those startling records in her father's notes: "The one who possesses the Tianji Record seizes creation between heaven and earth, peers into the mysteries of fate. Yet one who peers into heaven shall surely be counterattacked by heaven, and the record-holder shall ultimately become abandoned." She didn't speak these words, only nodded. "Agreed. But I have one condition too." Her voice was very calm. "Before the matter of the Forbidden Grounds is clarified, you cannot act alone. Any discovery must be reported to me immediately."

text.content: Chen Ji smiled slightly. This condition was far more lenient than he had expected. Obviously Su Qingyao was more eager for cooperation than he was—ten years of obsession had made her forget to weigh gains and losses too carefully. However, that flash of sharpness in her eyes made Chen Ji secretly take note: Su Qingyao was not someone who would be swayed by emotions. Even facing such a huge temptation, she remained calm. This woman was worth being wary of, and worth cooperating with. "Deal." He extended his hand. Su Qingyao looked at his hand, and after a moment, also extended hers. The two palms met lightly under the moonlight.

dialogue.content: The handshake lasted only a moment before they separated. Su Qingyao stepped back, resuming her cold and distant demeanor, as if nothing had happened moments before. "In three days, there will be a small council meeting in the Inner Sect to discuss countermeasures for the Jiazi Great Catastrophe. The position of Pavilion-Keeping Elder is currently vacant, and it's a time when capable people are needed." Her words were calm, but the meaning was clear—she intended to arrange Chen Ji's entry into that circle. "Thank you, junior sister." Chen Ji slightly cupped his hands. "Don't thank me." Su Qingyao turned, her skirt brushing across the stone tiles. "I just don't want my father's death to become an eternal unsolved mystery." Her figure gradually merged into the depths of the bamboo grove, leaving only a meaningful sentence echoing in the night wind:

choices.description: Revealing too many trump cards now is too dangerous. Su Qingyao may be formidable, but her ten-year obsession with investigating is itself the greatest variable. Binding too closely with her might make us a target for her enemies.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain an air of mystery, continue lurking under the identity of a废物
choices.risk_hint: Potentially thoroughly offending Su Qingyao, turning her from a potential ally into an enemy

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then slowly shook his head. "I appreciate Junior Sister Su's kindness, but let me consider the matter of cooperation." His tone was calm, showing neither hostility nor enthusiasm. "What we discussed tonight is enough for me to investigate certain matters. As for cooperation—" He slightly tilted his head, revealing a bitter smile. "An Outer Disciple/Servant cooperating with the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow? If this got out, it probably wouldn't sound good for the junior sister's reputation."

dialogue.content: A subtle change crossed Su Qingyao's eyes. She hadn't expected to be rejected—with her status and strength, extending an olive branch to an Outer Disciple/Servant was already a tremendous condescension. Yet the other party still needed to "consider"? Her pride almost made her want to turn and leave. But she restrained herself. Because she saw something familiar in this man—a caution and suspicion unique to those who have walked alone in darkness for too long. Wasn't she the same? "Very well." Her voice returned to its usual coldness. "Within three days, I will contact you again. If your answer is still a refusal—" She paused. "Then consider tonight never happened."

text.content: With that, she turned and left, her green figure quickly disappearing into the depths of the bamboo grove. Chen Ji stood in place, watching the direction she departed, his smile gradually fading. He knew she hadn't gone far—with Su Qingyao's personality, she would definitely double back to secretly observe his reaction. This was a test. A test about "how a废物 Outer Disciple/Servant would behave after refusing the invitation of an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow." If he showed even a trace of regret or anxiety, she would know that everything tonight was his performance. And if he appeared indifferent... that would be the normal reaction. Chen Ji smiled at the empty air, then turned and walked in the opposite direction, his steps unsteady, his back view lonely and dejected, perfectly portraying a self-pitying废物 Outer Disciple/Servant rejected by an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow. Acting this kind of role was his specialty.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's expression instantly became extremely complex. "Your father..." she said quietly. "Chen Xuan. Ten years ago, he served as the Outer Disciple Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect, the most promising candidate to inherit the sect leader position in the previous generation. But fifteen years ago, he disappeared during a sect mission, and everyone thought he was dead." She stared at Chen Ji. "Until three months ago, when I saw a portrait in the private notes of the Pavilion-Keeping Elder—a young man in that portrait who looked almost exactly like you. Beside the portrait was a line of text: 'The seventh-generation inheritor of the Tianji Record, must be eliminated.'"

text.content: Must be eliminated. A buzzing sound echoed in Chen Ji's mind. He knew his father died from an "accident," knew there was something fishy behind that "accident," but he didn't know—that his father was also an inheritor of the Tianji Record. Which meant he wasn't the seventh generation, but the eighth. Who killed his father? Why did the Pavilion-Keeping Elder's notes say "must be eliminated"? And the more critical question—Su Qingyao's father, the Su family's position in Tianqing Sect, was obviously deeply involved in this. "Your father and my father," Chen Ji slowly spoke. "What exactly did they discover ten years ago?"

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao shook her head, a flash of pain in her eyes: "I don't know. My father told me nothing. He only asked me to remember the person with the surname Chen." She took a deep breath. "But three months ago, after the Pavilion-Keeping Elder met with misfortune, I obtained his private notes. The notes mentioned that the seventh-level Forbidden Grounds of Tianqing Sect seal an ancient relic—the 'Heavenly Secrets Fragment,' which is the parent text of the Tianji Record. And the key to opening the seal is the bloodline of the 'Tianji Record Inheritor.'"

text.content: Chen Ji's heart suddenly sank. The parent text of the Tianji Record. The key to opening the seal. His bloodline. All of this connected, pointing to a possibility that made his spine grow cold—his father didn't die from an "accident" but was silenced. Because he possessed the bloodline to open the forbidden grounds' seal, and certain people didn't want the seal opened. Or in other words—certain people wanted to use this bloodline for something, but were interrupted by his father's resistance. So they killed his father, then began searching for the next person with this bloodline. And now, they've set their sights on him. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind: "Kid, your father discovered this secret too back then. He chose a path—destroying the Tianji Record, cutting off the possibility of bloodline inheritance. But you didn't follow his path; you chose to continue using it." He paused. "So the situation you face is more dangerous than your father faced back then."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao didn't notice Chen Ji's moment of distraction. She took out a yellowed piece of paper from her sleeve and handed it to Chen Ji: "This was something tucked inside the Pavilion-Keeping Elder's notes. I don't know what it means, but it mentions a date—the full moon night three months from now, when the Jiazi Great Catastrophe and the loosening of the forbidden grounds' seal overlap." She looked at Chen Ji, her eyes carrying a pleading expression. "I need an ally. Someone like me who wants to find the truth. Are you willing?"

text.content: Moonlight fell on the bamboo leaves, making a soft rustling sound. Su Qingyao stood before him, taking off the cold mask of the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow for the first time, revealing her ten-year obsession and loneliness without reservation. Chen Ji looked at her and suddenly remembered something Mo Xiansheng had once said: "The most dangerous thing in this world isn't enemies, but strangers with a common enemy. Because they trust each other too easily and betray each other too easily." But at this moment, he was willing to take this risk. Not because of trust, but because—they had no other choices.

Su Qingyao watched him quietly, waiting for his answer. Under the moonlight, her profile was like an exquisitely carved jade sculpture, cold and resolute. But Chen Ji noticed her fingers gripping the sword hilt were slightly white—that was the courage to still choose to believe after ten years of countless disappointments. "Alright." Chen Ji spoke, his voice soft but firm. "But I have one condition—whatever we find, we share. What you discover about my father, I want to know. What I discover about your father, you must also know." A complex light flashed in Su Qingyao's eyes, then she nodded: "Deal."

"There's one more thing." Before leaving, Su Qingyao suddenly stopped, turning to look at Chen Ji, her voice carrying a softness she herself hadn't noticed. "What you did in the scripture repository three months ago—the Pavilion-Keeping Elder survived until today because you drew away that wave of demonic energy. This matter, I've noted it down." She paused. "If you need help with anything in the future, come find me." With that, her figure, light as when she came, silently disappeared into the depths of the bamboo grove. Chen Ji stood in place, watching the direction she vanished, the corners of his mouth slightly rising. The first ally, acquired. Although she still suspected him, she had chosen to stand on his side. That was enough. The night wind blew past, carrying a hint of bamboo leaf fragrance. He looked down at the Tianji Record in his sleeve, the characters on the fragment shimmering with a light brighter than ever. Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded: "Kid, this is just the beginning. The Jiazi Great Catastrophe three months from now is the real chess game. And now, you've finally gained someone you can fight alongside—even if she doesn't know yet what kind of abyss she's about to step into."

Su Qingyao's figure vanished into the depths of the bamboo grove, leaving only one sentence that sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine—"Your father asked me the same question back then." The familiarity in that tone made Chen Ji feel for the first time a coldness beyond the chessboard. She knew his father. And she had hidden it for ten years.
